# 3 tips for shopping locally and finding unique gifts this holiday season


Shopping locally is a way to give much-needed support to independent businesses in your community while finding unique gifts for everyone on your holiday shopping list. Here are strategies for accomplishing both this season.


By


[Eric Best](https://stories.wf.com/author/eric-best/) ,


Staff Writer


## Key takeaways


- **Make an impact:** While businesses of all sizes may rely on the holiday season, finding gifts at local, independent businesses is especially important for the success of these smaller operations, survey data shows.
- **Ways you can shop locally:** Consider experiences over physical gifts, find events with many independent entrepreneurs, and think about giving a second life to a vintage present.
- **How to you can start:** Finding independent local businesses can be as simple as attending local market events or festivals, searching for secondhand or thrift stores, or buying gift cards from your favorite services or hospitality businesses.


Every holiday season, gift shopping can feel like a mad dash, but a little intention behind what you and your family buy this year could make a big difference in your community.


Where you shop matters, especially for local businesses. While small businesses make up[99.99% of businesses across the country](https://advocacy.sba.gov/2026/02/03/frequently-asked-questions-about-small-business-2026/) , they’re only expected to see about 43% of the $278 billion consumers are projected to spend this holiday season, according to an[Intuit QuickBooks survey](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/r/small-business-data/holiday-shopping-survey/) .


“We see firsthand how much the holiday shopping season matters for many of our customers. It’s a big part of their success,” said Dennis Devine, head of Wells Fargo Business Banking. “This time of year is important for every business, but when you choose gifts from independent stores and local entrepreneurs, it can make an even bigger difference in your community.”


Here’s why you should shop locally this year, making the holiday season of small business owners a little brighter in the process.


## 3 ways you can support local businesses this holiday season


### **Think outside the gift box**


Some gifts, especially from local businesses, aren’t meant to be wrapped, but that doesn’t mean they’ll have any less impact. Instead of a surprise that fits in a box, consider a gift card or voucher so a loved one can have a memorable meal or experience long after the holiday season.


Where should you go? Look beyond gifts shops. Think of favorite or special restaurants, arcades, nail salons, escape rooms, specialty stores for enthusiasts, and more. Adding a few of these businesses to your gift list won’t just mean making a loved one’s day — It’ll help a local entrepreneur, too.


### **Explore makers markets and gift fairs**


Buying local gifts doesn’t mean you have to skip the one-stop shopping convenience larger retailers are known for. Makers markets, craft shows, and other gift fairs offer opportunities to peruse the wares of many independent shops in a single trip. Oftentimes, makers at these events tailor their goods to holiday season shoppers.


Look on social media for events or peruse[online directories](https://www.fairsandfestivals.net/) ,[vendor maps](https://vendorsmap.com/) , or[databases](https://festivalnet.com/) to find one in your area. Farmers markets or flea markets may also have local business owners offering gifts.


### **Find secondhand or thrifted gifts**


You might already take part in the[circular economy](https://stories.wf.com/our-impact/circular-economy-can-reduce-what-you-throw-away/) without even knowing it. When you shop for used or secondhand gifts, such as thrifting vintage clothes, furniture, or housewares, you’re not only likely to be[more sustainable](https://www.forbes.com/sites/pamdanziger/2025/09/15/secondhand-goes-mainstream-as-more-shoppers-turn-to-thrift-and-online-resale/) , you’re also more likely to be supporting a small business in your community, too.


Many secondhand stores are[independent or regional](https://www.thethriftshopper.com/) . Used books, board or video games, clothes or jewelry, and other secondhand items are often cheaper or more unique than other gift options.


## 3 reasons why shopping locally matters to recipients, businesses, and communities


### **Finding great gifts for those on your holiday shopping list**


Many of us want to shop locally — whether it’s because we want to find that unique, extra-special gift or we’re looking for a last-minute present.


Nearly nine in 10 (89%) of surveyed shoppers say it’s important to support small businesses over other retailers, according to the Intuit QuickBooks survey. Their reasons? Finding unique or high-quality gifts (47%), supporting their community (46%), better customer service (38%), and convenience (33%).


### **Supporting local businesses at a crucial time**


Shopping locally doesn’t have to be seasonal, but the holiday season happens to be an important moment for many businesses. Small business owners may expect the shopping season to make up for an unstable year or slower sales during other seasons.


In fact, the holiday season is important for the overall profitability of about eight in 10 small businesses (79%), according to the U.S. Chamber of Commerce[Small Business Index](https://www.uschamber.com/small-business/keep-it-local-the-power-of-shopping-small-this-season) .


### **Investing in jobs and families in your community**


When you spend money with a locally owned business, more of that purchase price may stay within your community.


Research shows that purchases at these local independent stores create a ripple effect in their communities by returning more than three times as much money — from your purchase — into the local economy as larger chain competitors, according to the[American Independent Business Alliance](https://lsbe.d.umn.edu/articles/shop-local) .


“It’s not just what we buy that matters, but where, too. Many consumers are looking for ways to make purchases that align with their values,” Devine said. “When you give a gift from a local entrepreneur, it’s going to have an extra message behind it because you made that decision with intention.”
